chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir said:

Atiyyah said to me: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'I will perform Hajj alone (Ifrad), let me be your ransom, in one year.' He said to me: 'Even if you had performed a thousand [Hajjis] by performing Tamattu', do not perform Ifrad.'

key_terms.أُفْرِدُ الْحَجَّ: Performing Hajj al-Ifrad (performing Hajj alone without Umrah)
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: Let me be your ransom (a phrase of respect)
key_terms.سَنَةً: In one year / a single year
key_terms.فَتَمَتَّعْتَ: You had performed Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Hajj al-Ifrad and Hajj al-Tamattu' according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Atiyyah al-Akbar asks Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) whether he should perform Hajj al-Ifrad exclusively. The Imam’s response, 'Even if you performed a thousand [Hajjis] via Tamattu', should not perform Ifrad,' is interpreted by Shia jurists as either a strong recommendation (istihbab) for Tamattu' or a ruling of superiority, reflecting the prevalent view that Tamattu' is the most complete form of Hajj for those who can afford the sacrifice.
